subject: Request: bridge coverage endorsement to cover post-report gap — Elysian Health
messages:
From: Alex Stein <alex.stein@elysianhealth.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwoodai.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@elysianhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Gap coverage request for SOC 2 report (Dec 31, 2025 -> present)

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the SOC 2 Type II report you shared last month. Our compliance reviewers have one remaining item before we can move the contract forward: a short bridge/endorsement letter that covers the period between the report end date (2025-12-31) and the current date. Specifically they want:

- A dated statement confirming there have been no material changes to the control environment since 2025-12-31, or a clear description of any changes and compensating controls.
- Confirmation of the specific controls in scope (user access, change management, incident response) are still operational as documented.
- An executed letter (PDF) we can file with our procurement team; if you have a DocuSign flow that works, that would be ideal.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide this and — if so — when we might expect it? KPMG will accept a vendor-signed bridge letter for interim coverage.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alex Stein
Head of Procurement, Elysian Health
alex.stein@elysianhealth.com
attachments: 20260315-soc2-report-redwood-2025-type2.pdf (PDF, 4.2MB)

From: evelyn_hart@redwoodai.com
To: Alex Stein <alex.stein@elysianhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwoodai.com, priyom_das@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gap coverage request for SOC 2 report (Dec 31, 2025 -> present)

Alex — thanks for the note and for flagging the procurement requirement. We can provide a bridge coverage endorsement that addresses the three bullets you listed.

Marcus (Security) and Priyom (Legal) are looped in to draft and review the language. Two quick clarifying asks so we prepare exactly what you need:

1) Do you require KPMG to countersign the bridge letter, or will a Redwood-signed letter referencing the KPMG report suffice?
2) Is there a specific date you need the document filed by for your contracting timeline?

Tentative plan: Marcus will produce a short technical statement confirming control continuity (or note any changes). Priyom will review for contractual language and sign-off. We’ll target an initial draft within two weeks and a final, signed PDF with DocuSign if that’s acceptable.

I’ll be the primary contact on this. Thanks — we’ll prioritize.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: bridge endorsement language for Elysian Health

Evelyn / Priyom — attaching a draft bridge letter for Elysian. High-level notes:

- We have no material changes to the scoped controls (user access, change mgmt, incident response) since 2025-12-31.
- There were routine personnel rotations on the infra team (Jan/Feb 2026) but all access reviews and role reassignments were performed and documented; no privilege escalation incidents.
- There is one planned platform maintenance window scheduled for May 2026 (already communicated to customers) that does not affect control objectives.

Action items before sending externally:
- Priyom: please review the legal phrasing and confirm signatory block.
- Evelyn: confirm Elysian will accept Redwood-signed letter without KPMG countersign. If they require countersign, we need to coordinate with KPMG (they have offered to advise but not routinely countersign vendor-issued bridges).

Attachment: 20260414-bridge-draft-elysian.docx (Word, 28KB)

-Marcus
Director, Security Engineering
